findings.title: Backup-code branch allows login without password verification
findings.body: In `authorize()` the password is only verified when `credentials.totpCode` is empty (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` at line 121). The new backup-code branch at line 131 is evaluated for `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` regardless of whether a password was checked, and it takes precedence over the TOTP branch. A request that sends any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "000000") together with a valid `backupCode` therefore skips password verification entirely and also never validates the TOTP code, so the backup code alone grants a session. Backup codes are meant to be a second factor (they are even downloaded to a plain text file / copied to the clipboard), so this turns a leaked backup code into a full account takeover. The backup-code path should require successful password verification before accepting the code.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The code decrypts `user.backupCodes`, nulls the matched entry in memory and writes the whole re-encrypted array back with `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent login attempts using the same backup code can both read the array before either writes, so the same single-use code is accepted twice. Likewise, two concurrent logins using two different codes will each write back their own copy of the array, and the last write resurrects the code consumed by the other request. Consuming the code should be done atomically (e.g. inside a transaction with a conditional update / row lock) so a code can be redeemed exactly once.

findings.title: Unvalidated backupCode body field can crash the endpoint
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes the field is a string. A client sending a non-string JSON value (number, array, object) makes the handler throw a TypeError, which surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 validation error. The same pattern exists for `credentials.backupCode` in next-auth-options.ts. The field should be validated (type and expected format) before use. Also note `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is unguarded and will throw a 500 if the stored value cannot be decrypted/parsed.

findings.title: "missing_backup_codes" message points to a settings flow that does not exist
findings.body: The new string `missing_backup_codes` says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." but there is no UI anywhere in this PR to generate or regenerate backup codes: codes are only created inside `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup`, which rejects users who already have 2FA enabled (`TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`). Every user who enabled 2FA before this change (and any user who closed the dialog without saving the codes) will hit this error and will be told to do something that is impossible without first disabling 2FA. Either add a regeneration endpoint/UI or change the message to tell the user to disable and re-enable 2FA.

findings.title: Assertion on the 2FA switch is a no-op and is left unfixed
findings.body: `expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the unawaited Promise returned by `isChecked()`, which is always truthy, so the first test never verifies that 2FA was actually enabled (the PR adds a FIXME acknowledging this instead of fixing it). With the new backup-codes step inserted into the flow this assertion is the only post-enable check in that test, so a regression in the enable flow would not be caught. Use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` or the `[data-state="checked"]` locator as the second test does.

findings.title: No test covers logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The core new behaviour of this PR — authenticating with a backup code in `next-auth-options.ts` (including single-use consumption) and in the disable endpoint — has no automated coverage; the added test only clicks the download/copy/close buttons on the new dialog and the file notes this as a TODO. Regressions such as a code being reusable, or the "Lost access" flow sending the wrong field, would go undetected.

findings.title: Dismissing the backup-codes dialog skips onEnable(), leaving the parent UI stale
findings.body: 2FA is already enabled on the server when the `DisplayBackupCodes` step is shown, but `onEnable()` is only called by the "Close" button. If the user dismisses the dialog with the X / Escape / overlay (which goes through `onOpenChange`), the parent's enable callback never runs, so the two-factor switch and any cached profile data keep showing 2FA as disabled until a reload, and the user loses the codes without any warning. The enable callback should also run when the dialog is closed from this step.
